children: A budgeted BFS from a root Document over the Content Edges Table — published-only, depth-clamped, and the source of the root the Graph Renderer pins.

Graph Traversal is a breadth-first search starting from a root Document. It expands outward over from_id/to_id edges in the Content Edges Table, including reverse expansion via the reverse_referencers helper (the same one Blast Radius uses), so the graph shows both what a node links to and what links to it.
The walk is deliberately bounded so a hub document can't blow up a request:

content. An edge into an unpublished or deleted target doesn't resolve — instead of a real node, the walk emits a Phantom Node for that Dangling Reference. A node reached with no onward edges within budget is effectively a leaf; a Document with no edges at all is an Orphan Node and is never reached by traversal at all.

Where Search retrieves ranked nodes for a query, traversal retrieves connected nodes for a root — graph and search are two reads of one corpus, which is why a Search note bridges naturally here. Both expose their results through HTTP API v1; traversal's edges come from /v1/graph.
